images.caption: Grassmillees Farm The farm lies on the side of the B705 from Mauchline to Cumnock via Catrine and Auchinleck. Some of the land of this farm has been given up for the development of private housing on the outskirts of Mauchline. The land being developed offers, at present, almost unrestricted views to the south over the Mauchline basin.

images.caption: Junction of B705 with A76(T) The War memorial stands on an 'island' between the entrance and exit from and to the A76(T) road from the B705. images.caption: Kay's curling stone factory Only curling stone making factory in Scotland. Granite slabs in foreground were quarried on Ailsa Craig, an island in the Firth of Clyde.  The circular holes in the granite slab in the foreground show where the granite for two stones have been removed. The rock from Ailsa Craig is an example of a microgranite.
images.alt: Kay's curling stone factory Only curling stone making factory in Scotland. Granite slabs in foreground were quarried on Ailsa Craig, an island in the Firth of Clyde.  The circular holes in the granite slab in the foreground show where the granite for two stones have been removed. The rock from Ailsa Craig is an example of a microgranite.

images.caption: Local sawmill Sawmill mainly producing materials for the local farming community e.g. fence posts. It uses the former site of sandstone quarries which produced the once famous Ballochmyle sandstone. The sandstone was formed under desert conditions and fossilised sand dunes, of possibly Permian age, were found in the quarries until they were filled in during the latter decades of the 20th century.

images.caption: Loudon Street  shops The village is well provided with a variety of shops. 2 of the three main supermarkets are found here. There is also a family butcher, chemist, photographer,hardware store,sports shop, hair salon, tearoom/baker, greengrocer,a fashion and clothing shop as well as the Post Office and Newsagent.

images.caption: Loudoun Street, Mauchline This is the main shopping area in the village and is part of the B743 which links Mauchline to the town of Ayr. Traffic congestion can be a problem in what is one of the original streets in the village.

images.caption: Cheese Packing Factory This was formerly a Scottish Milk Marketing Board creamery which was the collection centre for milk from the local dairy farms. It used this milk for  a large number of dairy manufacturing processes e.g. butter making. Due to the restructuring of the Milk Marketing Board activities in south west Scotland and a reduction in the volume of milk produced locally, a number of these manufacturing processes have been lost to the factory, leaving cheese packing as the main activity.

images.caption: Eroded floodplain The R.Ayr is entering a gorge section here with very steep walls cut into red sandstone rock on the wooded right hand side of the photograph.
